viewer_rsvp.description: What the viewer has answered: going, maybe, or left out.

definition.description: What it shows, as its owner set it (feeds.md).

icon.description: The name of the icon its owner chose for it.

Image.description: Image is one size of a picture.

ImageSize.description: ImageSize is how big an image is.

LimitedActor.description: LimitedActor is what somebody is shown of a profile they may not see, when that profile lets people ask to follow it: enough to know whose it is and to ask.

allow_follow_request.description: Whether it lets people ask to follow it. False for one shown only because the viewer was invited.

body.description: And what it is, for the same reason. Only with Event.

event.description: On an event the viewer was invited to: when it is, so they can decide. Never where to join it online.

is_follow_requested_by_viewer.description: Whether the viewer has asked already and is waiting.

is_invited.description: Whether the viewer has been invited to follow it and is yet to answer.

restricted.description: Always true. What tells a client this is not the profile itself.

via_host.description: An event that lets in the followers of the group hosting it, shown to one of them. They can answer it as it stands, going or maybe.

gone.description: They are not where they came from any more either: the post was taken away there, or its server is gone.

abusereport.ProfileCase.description: ProfileCase is a case as a group's or an event's administrators see it (roadmap row 102, part 6b): what was reported and the reports against its rules, never who made them, nor the site's decision notes.

reports.description: The reports against the profile's rules, oldest first.

target.description: Target is the reported node as it is now, or absent when it is gone.

target_gone.description: Whether what was reported is gone.

target_id.description: The id of what was reported.

target_type.description: What kind of node it is.

abusereport.ProfileReport.description: ProfileReport is one report against a profile's rules, with nobody's name.

rule.description: The rule broken, by its title.

abusereport.Reason.description: Reason is one entry of the list a reporter chooses from, in their language.

key.description: What it is called in a report.

label.description: What it is called, in the language asked for.

requires_details.description: Whether the reporter must say more in their own words.

abusereport.ReasonCount.description: ReasonCount is how many reports in a case gave one reason.

abusereport.Report.description: Report is one person's report, as an administrator sees it.

rule.description: With reason_key "rule": the rule broken, by its title, and whose rule it is, 0 for the site's.

rule_profile.description: The group or event whose rule it is.

updated_at.description: When it was last changed: a second report by the same person updates it.

activitypub.Actor.description: Actor is somebody, as they are described to another server.

manuallyApprovesFollowers.description: Whether a follow waits to be approved.

activitypub.Collection.description: Collection is a list said only by how long it is: who follows somebody is theirs to know, and how many is all that is told.

activitypub.JRD.description: JRD is a WebFinger answer: who a handle is, and where they are.

activitypub.Note.description: Note is a post, as it is sent to and read from another server.

attachment.description: The pictures of a photo post, or the video of a video post.

inReplyTo.description: What it answers, by the address that has between servers.

location.description: Where it is: the first location its author chose for it, a `Place` (roadmap row 82, part 3b). Every one is also a `Place` in Tag.

name.description: An Article's title, and the opening it is summed up by. A note has neither: Mastodon shows a note's summary as a warning to click past.

activitypub.RemotePerson.description: RemotePerson is somebody on another server, as the web app is told.

alias.description: Their handle: alice@mastodon.example.

locked.description: Whether a follow of theirs waits to be approved.

type.description: Always the type of a person on the fediverse.

uri.description: Their address between servers, and the server it is on.

url.description: Their page on their own server.

activitypub.SentIcon.description: SentIcon is a still that stands for a video.

activitypub.SentPicture.description: SentPicture is one picture of a post, as it is sent: where to fetch it, what it is, how big, and what its author said it shows.

icon.description: A video's poster, which Mastodon shows before it plays.

activitypub.Settings.description: Settings is what a person is shown about being on the fediverse.

available.description: Whether they could be, and why not when they could not.

handle.description: What they are, or would be, called from other servers, and where those servers find them.

activitypub.Tag.description: Tag names somebody or a hashtag that a post mentions, beside its text, or a location it was tagged with, a `Place` with its point.

actor.GroupDeletionCounts.description: GroupDeletionCounts is what deleting a group or an event would take with it, for the Danger zone.

member_since.description: When it was made, when it is known.

actor.HandleResponse.description: HandleResponse is which profile an alias is: where the web app reads it, and by what.

alias.description: Its alias, as it is kept.

kind.description: "people", "groups" or "events": the profile's own address begins so.

actor.PersonDeletionCounts.description: PersonDeletionCounts is what deleting a person would take with it, for the Danger zone.

member_since.description: When they joined, when it is known.

access.description: Who may see it: `public`, `registered`, `followers`, `leaders`, `mutuals`, `admins` or `myself` (permissions.md).

alias.description: Its handle (`ana`, or `ana@mastodon.social` for somebody on another server).

allow_download.description: What this actor's new photos and videos start with: whether they may be downloaded.

allow_follow_request.description: Whether people its profile is not open to may ask to follow it.

archived_at.description: Permanent, and set only once archived, so the settings page can show the state rather than offering an action that no longer applies.

avatar_urls.description: Its picture, in each size there is: `small`, `medium`, `large`, `square`.

cover_urls.description: Its cover picture, in each size there is: `medium`, `large`.

deleted_at.description: Present only while the actor is scheduled for deletion, so the settings page can offer Restore instead of the delete form. Deleting also clears Enabled, and a client reading only that cannot tell an account on its way out from one an administrator disabled.

enabled.description: Whether it is enabled: false when a site administrator has disabled it, or while it is being deleted.

event.description: On an event: when it is, how many may go and are going, and what the viewer answered. Left out on anything else.

featured_at.description: Set only while the installation features this actor, so a super administrator's profile menu can show the toggle's state.

is_admined_by_viewer.description: Whether the viewer is one of its administrators.

is_blocked_by_viewer.description: Whether the viewer has blocked it.

is_invited.description: Whether the viewer has been invited to follow this actor and is yet to answer.

language.description: The language this person usually posts in. Left out when not set.

origin_domain.description: The server it came from, when it came from another.

quote_policy.description: On a person: who may quote their posts, when a post does not say. "anyone", "followers" or "nobody"; left out when they have not said, which is anyone.

show_reposts_on_profile.description: Whether what this actor reposts is also among its profile's posts.

type.description: What kind of profile it is: `node.actor.actor-service.person.v1`, `...group.v1` or `...event.v1`, or one of another server's.

uri.description: What it is called on the server it came from, and that server, when it came from another. Left out of everything made here.

verified.description: A mark kept from earlier versions of Anahita. Nothing sets it yet.

website_url.description: One link on the profile. Rendered as an anchor, so the value is validated to http(s) on the way in — see requests/actor.go.

actor.Rule.description: Rule is one of a profile's rules.

body.description: A line more, if it needs one.

title.description: A few words: "Be kind".

actor.Rules.description: Rules is a profile's rules, as they are now.

agreed_version.description: The version the viewer last agreed to, 0 for none: behind Version, they are asked again.

updated_at.description: When they last changed, RFC 3339, or empty.

version.description: Raised by every change; 0 for a profile that never had any.

actor.TaggedPerson.description: TaggedPerson is one person in a post, as the post's list of them answers.

pending.description: Waiting for their approval: shown only to them and the post's author.

atproto.ImportPreview.description: ImportPreview is what following here whoever the viewer follows on Bluesky would do, before it is done.

following.description: How many accounts the viewer follows on Bluesky.

most.description: The most followed here in one go.

posts_of_each.description: How many of each one's latest posts are read.

atproto.ImportStarted.description: ImportStarted says following them here has begun: it carries on after the answer, and for a long list takes minutes.

atproto.RemotePerson.description: RemotePerson is somebody on Bluesky, as the web app is told. The same shape as somebody found on the fediverse.

alias.description: Their handle: alice.bsky.social.

locked.description: Nobody on Bluesky approves who follows them.

type.description: Always a Bluesky person's type.

uri.description: Their address between servers, and where they are kept as from.

atproto.Settings.description: Settings is somebody's connection to Bluesky, as the web app is told.

broken.description: The account's server no longer takes what was kept: it has to be connected again.

admin_count.description: Groups, events and websites only: how many administrators it has.

alias.description: The username.

content_count.description: How many posts it has written.

deleted_at.description: When it was deleted, while it waits out the thirty days before it is purged; absent otherwise.

email_verified.description: People only: whether they confirmed their address.

onboarded.description: People only: whether they went through the walk-through after signing up.

state.description: `active`, `disabled`, `archived` or `deleted` (on its way to being destroyed).

tier.description: `empty`: nothing written, following nobody and followed by nobody; `dormant`: not active for as long as the installation calls dormant (`ACCOUNT_DORMANT_DAYS`); `active` otherwise.

auth.Agreements.description: Agreements is what somebody has accepted of the two documents.

city.description: Roughly where it began, from its address. Empty when not known.

client_id.description: The app it signed in to.

id.description: The session's id: what signing it out names.

is_active.description: Whether it is still signed in.

is_viewer.description: Whether it is the session asking.

auth.CodeMismatch.description: CodeMismatch refuses a wrong code, and says how many tries are left before it stops working.

auth.ConfirmationMismatch.description: ConfirmationMismatch refuses a confirmation that names another number than there is now.

total.description: How much is public now: what to confirm instead.

auth.InviteItem.description: InviteItem is an invitation, as its sender sees it. Not the link: that is in the mail that was sent, and nowhere else.

id.description: Its id: what taking it back names.

auth.InviteList.description: InviteList is a page of the viewer's invitations, and how many of them are waiting.

pagination.description: Where this page is among all of them.

pending.description: How many are waiting: sent, and not yet accepted, expired or taken back. The most that may wait is the viewer's entitlement, in userinfo (`entitlements.invites.max_pending`); sending another at it is refused (`too_many_invitations`).

auth.Item.description: Item is one rule, promise or suggestion: a short title, and a line more if it needs one.

auth.JWKSet.description: JWKSet is the keys a token's signature is checked with (RFC 7517).

keys.description: Each a JSON Web Key: `kid`, `kty`, `alg`, `use`, `n` and `e`.

auth.NodeInfoDocument.description: NodeInfoDocument is what the installation is (NodeInfo 2.1).

metadata.description: What the web app reads of the installation: `nodeName`, `nodeDescription`, `logoUrl`, `registrationMode`, `approvalRequired`, `invitationsAccepted`, `invitesFrom`, `groupsFrom`, `eventsFrom`, `websitesFrom`, `locationsFrom`, `minContentAccess`, `readAccess`, `networks`, `photoMaxFiles`, `siteRules`, `spamRemovalMaxDays`, `accountGraceDays`, `videoUploads`, `videoMaxBytes`, `videoMaxSeconds`, `animationMaxBytes`, `animationMaxSeconds`, `termsOfServiceUrl`, `privacyPolicyUrl`, and the support contacts `supportEmail`, `supportPhone` and `supportWebsite`.

openRegistrations.description: Whether anybody may sign up without being invited or approved.

protocols.description: What it speaks with other servers: `activitypub`, when it federates.

auth.NodeInfoLinks.description: NodeInfoLinks is where the NodeInfo document is, for each version there is.

auth.OAuthClientCreatedItem.description: OAuthClientCreatedItem is the response shape used only on Add and RotateSecret — the plaintext client_secret is exposed once and never returned by any other endpoint.

active.description: Whether it may sign people in.

client_id.description: What it calls itself when it signs people in: a slug.

client_secret.description: Its secret, shown this once and never again. Empty for a public app.

confidential.description: Whether it can keep a secret: an app's own server can, an app in a browser or on a phone cannot.

first_party.description: Whether it is one of the installation's own apps.

id.description: Its number here: what the routes name it by.

name.description: What people are shown it is called.

redirect_uris.description: Where people may be sent back to after signing in. Exactly these.

scopes.description: What it may ask to do (oauth.md).

skip_consent.description: Whether people are not asked to allow it.

token_expiry.description: How long its access tokens last, in seconds.

active.description: Whether it may sign people in.

client_id.description: What it calls itself when it signs people in: a slug.

confidential.description: Whether it can keep a secret: an app's own server can, an app in a browser or on a phone cannot.

first_party.description: Whether it is one of the installation's own apps.

id.description: Its number here: what the routes name it by.

name.description: What people are shown it is called.

redirect_uris.description: Where people may be sent back to after signing in. Exactly these.

scopes.description: What it may ask to do (oauth.md).

skip_consent.description: Whether people are not asked to allow it.

token_expiry.description: How long its access tokens last, in seconds.

auth.OAuthErrorResponse.description: OAuthErrorResponse is the standard OAuth error response body per RFC 6749 §5.2.

error.description: Why, as RFC 6749 names it: `invalid_client`, `invalid_grant` and so on.

error_code.description: For a refused refresh token, which it was: `refresh_expired`, `refresh_not_found` and `refresh_reuse` end the session; `refresh_raced` does not, since another request refreshed first.

active.description: Whether it is live. Nothing else is said of one that is not.

client_id.description: The app it was issued to.

exp.description: When it expires, in seconds since 1970.

scope.description: What it may do, separated by spaces.

sub.description: Whose it is: the person's id, or the app's for its own.

auth.OAuthSigningKeyItem.description: OAuthSigningKeyItem is a key the installation signs tokens with, as an administrator sees it. Neither half of the key is sent: the public one is in the JWKS, and the private one never leaves the service.

active.description: Whether new tokens are signed with it. Tokens it signed are still verified while it is in the JWKS.

backend.description: Where the private key is kept: `local`, in the database, or `kms`.

expires_at.description: When it stops being signed with.

key_id.description: The `kid` a token names it by, in its header.

access_token.description: What a request is signed with: `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A JWT.

expires_in.description: How long the access token lasts, in seconds.

id_token.description: Who signed in, when `openid` was asked for (OpenID Connect).

refresh_token.description: What gets the next tokens when this one expires; used once. Not for an app acting for itself.

scope.description: What the tokens may do, separated by spaces.

auth.Onboarded.description: Onboarded says when the viewer went through the walk-through.

onboarded_at.description: The first time: calling again does not move it.

auth.OnboardingState.description: OnboardingState is what the walk-through needs that userinfo does not carry.

invited_by.description: The username of whoever invited the viewer, to show first. Null when nobody did, or they can no longer be followed.

auth.OpenIDConfiguration.description: OpenIDConfiguration is the OpenID Connect discovery document (OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0, section 3): where each endpoint is, and what the installation supports.

claims_supported.description: What a token or userinfo may say.

issuer.description: Who issues the tokens: the `iss` in each.

auth.PasskeyCount.description: PasskeyCount is how many passkeys somebody holds, and nothing else about them.

auth.PasskeySignedIn.description: PasskeySignedIn is where the browser goes next, now that it is signed in: back to the authorization that sent it to sign in, or to the app.

auth.PasskeysRevoked.description: PasskeysRevoked is how many passkeys were removed.

auth.PasswordChanged.description: PasswordChanged says how many other sessions were signed out.

revoked_sessions.description: Every one but the one that changed it.

auth.PersonTypeChanged.description: PersonTypeChanged is a person's type, and whether this changed it.

changed.description: False when they already had it.

auth.PublicContent.description: PublicContent is how much is public: on the installation, or changed by making it registered-only.

people.description: People whose profiles anybody may see.

public_allowed.description: Whether new public content is still allowed here. While it is, the conversion is refused: it would be undone by the next public post.

total.description: The three together: the number to confirm.

auth.Rules.description: Rules is the site's rules, with the version agreed to. Raising the version asks everybody to agree again; a correction that leaves it as it is asks nobody.

auth.SessionStarted.description: SessionStarted says the app's session holds its tokens now.

auth.SignupDecided.description: SignupDecided is the answer given to a request.

person_id.description: The account made, when it was approved.

auth.SignupRequestItem.description: SignupRequestItem is what an administrator sees.

id.description: The request's id: what answering it names.

invited_by.description: Who invited them, when somebody did: a person's id.

username_taken.description: UsernameTaken says whether the name they asked for is still free.

auth.SiteAbout.description: SiteAbout is what GET /site answers: every text in every language it is written in, keyed by the web app's language names ("en-CA", "fr-FR"), for the reader's app to choose from.

promises.description: Shown on the About page, under "Our promises to you".

rule_suggestions.description: Offered to a group's administrators when they write its rules.

rules.description: The site's rules, and the version agreed to: everybody ticks each before using the site, and again when the version is raised.

auth.TotpStatus.description: TotpStatus is whether somebody has two-factor authentication.

expired.description: Whether its last passcode is too long ago, so that signing in asks for one. Always false when it is off.

auth.UsernameChanged.description: UsernameChanged is the username as it was stored.

auth.WebAuthnCredentialItem.description: WebAuthnCredentialItem is the person-facing shape of an enrolled passkey.

clone_warning.description: Whether it looked copied when last used: worth removing.

id.description: Its id: what renaming or removing it names.

last_used_at.description: When it was last used. Null when never.

nickname.description: What it is called: the device, unless its owner renamed it.

synced.description: Whether it is kept in sync across devices, so that losing one loses nothing.

auth.consentItem.description: consentItem is one recorded acceptance, as a client sees it.

accepted_at.description: When. Null when they never have.

auth.nodeInfoLink.description: nodeInfoLink is where one version of the document is.

auth.nodeInfoServices.description: nodeInfoServices is what the installation bridges to and from: nothing.

inbound.description: Both are required by the schema and both are empty: this installation does not bridge to or from anything. They are `[]string{}` rather than nil because the schema says array, and a JSON null there makes strict consumers reject the whole document.

auth.nodeInfoSoftware.description: nodeInfoSoftware is what the installation runs.

auth.nodeInfoUsage.description: nodeInfoUsage is how much the installation is used.

auth.nodeInfoUsers.description: nodeInfoUsers is how many people have accounts.

activeHalfyear.description: Those active in the last six months.

activeMonth.description: Those active in the last month.

export.ExportItem.description: ExportItem is an export as its owner is told of it.

download_url.description: Where the archive is fetched from, while it is ready: an address good for a few minutes, made afresh each time this is read.

error.description: Why it failed, when it did.

expires_at.description: When the archive will be deleted.

size_bytes.description: How big the archive is, once it is ready.

export.ExportList.description: ExportList is the viewer's exports, and when they may ask again.

every_days.description: How many days must pass between two exports. 0 for no wait.

keep_days.description: How many days an archive is kept once it is ready.

next_at.description: When they may next ask, while they must wait.

export.TooSoon.description: TooSoon refuses an export asked for before it is time, and says when.

delete.description: Whether the viewer may delete it.

edit.description: Whether the viewer may change it.

pin.description: Keep it on the home page, and make a copy to change.

feed.CustomFeedPage.description: CustomFeedPage is a page of a custom feed's posts.

pagination.description: Where the page is.

feed.CustomFeedPagination.description: A feed is paged by what came before, and has no total: counting it would be reading all of it.

has_more.description: Whether there is a next page.

next_cursor.description: What to ask for as `cursor` for the next page.

feed.CustomFeedResponse.description: CustomFeedResponse is a feed as it is sent.

access.description: Who may see it.

authorized.description: What the viewer may do with it.

body.description: What it is for, in its owner's words.

is_pinned.description: Whether the viewer keeps it on their home page.

references.description: The profiles and places its definition names, the ones the viewer may see, for the editor to show by name. Sent with a single feed.

type.description: Always a custom feed's type.

feed.DiscoverPage.description: DiscoverPage is a page of the feeds people have shared.

pagination.description: Where the page is.

feed.DiscoverPagination.description: DiscoverPagination is where a page of shared feeds is: by how many came before it, and with no total.

has_more.description: Whether there is a next page.

next_start.description: What to ask for as `start` for the next page.

start.description: How many came before this page.

alias.description: What it is found by: `/hashtags/<alias>`.

followed.description: In the following and all lists: the viewer follows it.

name.description: The hashtag as it is shown, without its #.

profiles.description: In a trending list: how many profiles used it in the window, each once: the writers of posts carrying it, and the profiles tagged with it.

type.description: Always `node.tag.hashtag-service.hashtag.v1`.

uses.description: In the following and all lists: how many posts it is on that anybody may see, and the viewer's own.

hashtag.SuggestResponse.description: SuggestResponse is the hashtags offered, the best first.

hashtag.Suggestion.description: Suggestion is a hashtag in use, offered.

alias.description: In lower case: what it is found by, and what to write after the #.

followed.description: In one of the viewer's custom feeds.

uses.description: How many posts it is on that anybody may see, and the viewer's own.

linkpreview.PreviewResponse.description: PreviewResponse is a preview as it is sent: what the page says of itself.

description.description: What the page says of itself.

image.description: Where the picture is read from, on this installation.

site_name.description: The site it is on, as it calls itself.

title.description: What the page is called.

url.description: The link, as it was made plain before it was read.

location.LocationNodeItem.description: LocationNodeItem is a place posts can be tied to.

alias.description: Its short name.

authorized.description: What the viewer may do with it.

latitude.description: Where it is: latitude, found from its address.

profiles.description: In a trending list: how many profiles used it in the window, each once: the writers of posts tied to it, and the profiles tagged with it.

type.description: Always a place's type.

notification.MarkedRead.description: MarkedRead is how many notifications Mark all read marked.

count.description: How many were unread, and are read now.

notification.NotificationItem.description: NotificationItem is something the viewer is told of.

actions.description: What the viewer can do from it, now: `answer_request` (accept or decline a request to follow that is still waiting), `follow` (they do not follow whoever did it), `reply`. Left out when nothing.

comment_id.description: The reply or the repost that holds what was done, where it is not the object: the reply to answer, for a reply.

ids.description: Grouped with it (likes of one post, reposts of one post, follows of one profile): every notification's id, this one's first. Reading or deleting it is reading or deleting them all.

is_read.description: Whether the viewer has read it.

others.description: Whoever else did the same, newest first, at most two.

others_count.description: How many more did it than are named.

type.description: What it tells of, as the event that made it is named.

updated_at.description: When it last changed: when it was read, for one.

notification.Object.description: Object is what was done: a post, a reply, a like.

alias.description: Its handle, or its short name.

body.description: A profile's description. Left out on a post, whose words are its content.

name.description: A profile's name. Left out on a post, which has a title instead.

portrait_urls.description: A photo post's first picture, in each size there is.

title.description: A post's title, where it has one.

type.description: What kind of thing it is.

notification.Settings.description: Settings are what a person is told about, every kind of thing in order.

notification.Subject.description: Subject is who did what a notification tells of.

alias.description: Its handle, or its short name.

avatar_urls.description: Their picture, in each size there is.

type.description: What kind of thing it is.

notification.Target.description: Target is what it was done to: the viewer's post, or the viewer.

alias.description: Its handle, or its short name.

name.description: A profile's name. Left out on a post, which has a title instead.

title.description: A post's title, where it has one.

type.description: What kind of thing it is.

notification.TopicChoice.description: TopicChoice is whether a person is told about one kind of thing.

on.description: Whether they are told about it.

topic.description: The kind of thing: likes, reposts, replies, mentions, follows, posts, events or invitations.

notification.UnreadCount.description: UnreadCount is how many notifications the viewer has not read.

newest_at.description: When the newest of all their notifications, read or not, was told: changed, there is something new to fetch. Left out when they have none.

photo.FileRef.description: FileRef names one image a post is to have: one it has already, by its id, or one that was uploaded for it, by the upload's id.

alt_text.description: What it shows, for people who cannot see it.

id.description: An image the post has already, by its id.

upload_id.description: An image uploaded for it, by the upload's id.

photo.FilesRefusal.description: FilesRefusal says why a post's images were refused, and how many a post may have.

max.description: How many images a post may have.

photo.Uploaded.description: Uploaded is an image stored for a post that is not made yet.

upload_id.description: What the post names it by, in `uploads`.

urls.description: Each size made of it, as a post's pictures are sent.

recommendation.ActorsResponse.description: ActorsResponse is who the viewer might follow, and why.

related.description: What the reasons name, for saying them in words: the people who follow somebody suggested, the hashtags shared. The ones the viewer may see.

recommendation.Interest.description: Interest is a hashtag offered to pick, and on how many public posts it was lately.

alias.description: What it is found by.

count.description: How many posts it was on, lately.

name.description: The hashtag, as it is shown.

recommendation.PreferencesResponse.description: PreferencesResponse is somebody's choices as they are sent: with the weights they are ranked by, each reason there, and the service's own to go back to.

active_within_choices.description: What active_within_days may be, nearest first, and what it is for somebody who has not chosen.

active_within_days.description: How lately somebody must have been here to be suggested to them, in days. Nothing is no limit.

active_within_default.description: What active_within_days is for somebody who has not chosen.

discoverable.description: That they may be suggested to other people.

max_weight.description: The most a weight may be.

reasons.description: The reasons, in the order to list them.

suggest_people.description: To be suggested people, and groups.

use_activity.description: That what they liked and wrote may be used to choose for them.

weights.description: What each reason counts for, for the viewer, by its name.

recommendation.Reason.description: Reason is why a profile is suggested, as it is sent.

ids.description: Up to three of what it was found through: the people or the hashtags, named in the answer's `related`.

type.description: Which reason: `follows_you`, `followed_by_leaders`, `cited_by_leaders`, `inviter`, `hosted_by_leader`, `shared_interest`, `you_engaged`, `cited`, `popular` or `featured` (recommendations.md).

recommendation.SuggestionItem.description: SuggestionItem is one suggestion as it is sent: the profile, and why.

reasons.description: Why, the one that counted most first.

score.description: What it scored: higher is better.

search.PreferencesResponse.description: PreferencesResponse is the viewer's own steps for search's Most relevant: how much each sign that something was found useful counts for them, as a step that multiplies the installation's own weight.

adjustable.description: What may be set: `like`, `save`, `reply`, `follow`, `cite` and `following` (what the viewer follows coming first).

options.description: What each may be set to: 0 (off), 0.5, 1 (as is), 1.5 and 2.

steps.description: By name, what they have set; what is not here is 1, as the installation has it.
